title: OpenEXR Python RGB channel coalescing heap buffer overflow
summary: With default separate_channels=false, distinct RGB channel groups can coalesce to one Python binding key but have different component counts. The array is allocated for three components and a later four-component frame-buffer slice writes approximately 33% past the end when processing an untrusted OpenEXR file.
ai_role: The OpenEXR maintainer advisory states that Anthropic found this issue using Claude and that Ada Logics validated it. This supports case-specific AI-assisted discovery with independent human validation; the source does not specify Claude’s individual investigative steps or model version.
classification_note: The advisory documents the public disclosure and fix but does not establish whether defenders knew of the issue or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: The OpenEXR GHSA lists fixed release versions 3.3.15, 3.4.17, and 3.5.3. This records the upstream fix only; downstream packaging/deployment is not inferred.

impacts.conditions: A Python program must call OpenEXR.File with default arguments on an untrusted file. The advisory does not establish controlled code execution.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a file-crafted reproducer/attack condition; it does not report observed exploitation.
